Approval.description:
A human approval binding five pieces of evidence together (RX-05).

The record is frozen: an approval whose bound fields could be edited after
the fact would be an audit record that cannot be audited.

``approved_at`` must be supplied by the caller as a timezone-aware
``datetime``. This model never reads the clock -- a record that stamps
itself cannot be reconstructed from evidence or tested deterministically.

action_digest.description: Digest of the action this approval authorises, and no other.
action_digest.title: Action Digest

approval_id.description: Stable id of this approval record.
approval_id.title: Approval Id

approved_at.description: When the approval was given. Timezone-aware; supplied by the caller.
approved_at.title: Approved At

candidate_hash.description: Hash of the exact repair candidate approved (RX-06).
candidate_hash.title: Candidate Hash

contract_hash.description: Hash of the ResultContract this approval judges (RX-03).
contract_hash.title: Contract Hash

environment_policy_digest.description: Digest of the execution policy the run must obey (RX-08).
environment_policy_digest.title: Environment Policy Digest

input_snapshot_id.description: Id of the immutable input snapshot used (RX-01).
input_snapshot_id.title: Input Snapshot Id

Approval.title: Approval

ComparisonSpec.description: The comparison algorithm and its per-output tolerances (RX-03, RX-13).

tolerances.description: Output name -> tolerance. Keys must name declared outputs.
tolerances.title: Tolerances

ComparisonSpec.title: ComparisonSpec

ExclusionRule.description:
One explicit exclusion rule (RX-03, RX-14).

Exclusions are structured rather than free prose so that an altered
exclusion can be reported as a named methodology delta.

expression.description: Optional machine-checkable form of the rule. Not evaluated by this layer.
expression.title: Expression

rule_id.description: Stable id, unique within the contract.
rule_id.title: Rule Id

ExclusionRule.title: ExclusionRule

OutputDefinition.description:
One declared output of the workflow (RX-03, RX-13).

``unit`` is optional only for dimensionless or non-numeric outputs. When it
is present it must agree with the contract-level ``units`` mapping; a
contract that declares two different units for the same output is
self-contradictory and is refused (see :class:`ResultContract`).

kind.description: Output kind; decides which comparison is admissible.

name.description: Output name, unique within the contract.
name.title: Name

unit.description: Physical unit, or None for a dimensionless or non-numeric output.
unit.title: Unit

OutputDefinition.title: OutputDefinition

OutputKind.description:
What kind of thing a declared contract output is (RX-03, RX-13).

The kind decides which comparison is admissible. ``SCALAR``, ``VECTOR``,
``ARRAY`` and ``TABLE`` are numeric and therefore require a declared
tolerance; ``TEXT``, ``FIGURE`` and ``ARTEFACT`` are not numerically
comparable and are compared by exact content digest instead.

``ARTEFACT`` is the deliberate escape hatch for an opaque output. It is
closed-set-safe because an artefact carries no tolerance semantics: the
verifier can only say "identical bytes" or "different bytes", never
"close enough".
OutputKind.title: OutputKind

Population.description:
The expected population and how it is selected (RX-03, RX-14).

``expected_count`` is the row/record count the contract asserts. A
reproduction that produces a different count is a changed population, which
is a methodology delta (RX-14), not a numeric difference.

selection_rule.description: The rule by which records enter the population, stated explicitly.
selection_rule.title: Selection Rule

Population.title: Population

ReferenceInput.description:
One reference input pinned by content digest (RX-01, RX-03).

``path`` is snapshot-relative and traversal-free; ``sha256`` pins the exact
bytes, so "the contract's reference inputs" is a verifiable statement rather
than a filename convention.

path.description: Snapshot-relative path to the reference input.
path.title: Path

role.description: Why this input is referenced, e.g. 'raw-measurements' or 'reference-output'.
role.title: Role

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact reference bytes.
sha256.title: Sha256

ReferenceInput.title: ReferenceInput

SplitSpec.description:
A declared train/evaluation split (RX-03, RX-14).

``train_fraction`` is strictly between 0 and 1: a 'split' that assigns
everything to one side is not a split, and silently accepting 0.0 or 1.0
would let a contract declare a split it does not perform.

seed.description: Split seed, or None if not seeded.
seed.title: Seed

SplitSpec.title: SplitSpec

Tolerance.description:
Per-output comparison tolerance (RX-03, RX-13).

At least one of ``abs_tol`` / ``rel_tol`` must be declared. A tolerance
record with neither would mean "compare to no stated precision", which is
not a comparison, so it is refused. Non-finite and negative tolerances are
refused for the same reason: a tolerance of ``inf`` accepts everything.
Tolerance.title: Tolerance

description:
A versioned, hashed scientific declaration (RX-03, RX-04).

Invariants enforced at construction, each with a negative control in
``tests/contracts/test_result_contract.py``:

* ``known_limits`` is non-empty. A contract that states no limits is not
  acceptable: it claims the declaration has no boundary, which is never
  true of a real scientific result.
* ``output_definitions`` is non-empty. There is nothing to reproduce
  otherwise.
* output names, reference paths, exclusion ids and required check ids are
  each unique.
* every key of ``units`` and of ``comparison.tolerances`` names a declared
  output -- a tolerance for an output that does not exist is dead
  declaration that reads as coverage.
* ``units[name]`` agrees with that output's own ``unit`` when both are
  given (RX-13: unit mismatch is a failure, never a conversion).
* every numeric output has a declared tolerance; without one the verifier
  has no admissible comparison and would have to invent a threshold.

Immutability: sequence fields are ``tuple`` so they cannot be appended to
after construction. ``units`` and ``comparison.tolerances`` are ``dict``
because RX-03 specifies a mapping, and pydantic cannot freeze a dict in
place -- see :attr:`KNOWN_SHAPE_LIMITS`.

approval.description: Approval linkage (RX-04/RX-05). Excluded from contract_hash because an approval binds to that hash and cannot be inside it.

known_limits.description: What this contract does NOT establish. Must be non-empty.
known_limits.title: Known Limits

population.description: Expected record count and selection rule.

reference_inputs.description: Inputs that count as reference, pinned by digest (RX-01).
reference_inputs.title: Reference Inputs

required_checks.description: Ids of the checks a verification must run.
required_checks.title: Required Checks

seed.description: Seed, or None when none is declared.
seed.title: Seed

units.description: Output name -> unit. Keys must name declared outputs.
units.title: Units
